Check the number of turns between tap changes by cranking
 the tap changer from a raise to a lower and back to a raise position. The
 turns must not be greater than one. If the turns are greater than one use
 the following steps:
 a) Turn the crank handle clockwise from
 position 10 to position 9 until the diverter switch operates and count
 the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to appear in
 the green section in the middle of the inspection.
 b) Turn the crank handle counterclockwise
 from position 9 to position 10 until the diverter switch operates and
 count the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to
 appear in green section in the middle of the inspection glass.

c)
 Note the difference between the counted
 crank handle revolutions

d) To correct any revolutions greater than
 one by divided by 2 and turning the crank in the direction of the most
 turns after uncoupling the drive shaft.

e) Re-couple the motor drive at vertical part
 of the driving shaft

f) Repeat steps I and 2 to verify the same
 number of turns in each direction

Instructions for
Type V Tap changer Coupling
Check after Maintenance

Checking the Motor Drive coupling
after maintenance on the type V Tap changer

During maintenance of the tap changer the motor drive is
uncoupled to remove the tap changer. Because of this tests must be made to
ensure the tap changer operation is accomplished before the motor drive stops.
This operation is guaranteed by the quick action mechanism of the diverter
switch is released at a distinct interval before the end of the motor drive
operation. The intervals between the moment of release of the diverter switch
and the end of the motor drive action must be the same in both rotational
directions.

Equalizing the rotation lag is necessary if the number of
revolutions in clockwise and counterclockwise direction deviate form each other
by more than one rotation.

To accomplish this steps must be taken to check the rotation of
the drive in both lower and raise positions.

Turn the crank handle clockwise from position 10 to
 position 9 until the diverter switch operates and count the crank handle
 revolutions necessary for the red mark to appear in the green section in
 the middle of the inspection glass.

Turn the crank handle counterclockwise from position 9to
 position 10 until the diverter switch operates and count the crank handle
 revolutions necessary for the red mark to appear in the green section in
 the middle of the inspection glass.

Electrical and mechanical limit switches prevent the motor drive
from going past the end position. This is a critical test.

items:
The safety switch B8 must interrupt the motor and control
 circuit when the hand crank is inserted.

This test must be done during a period where B 12 or B 14 is
 switched on which means more than 2 digits from a permanent position.

Start MA7 performing an electrical operation. When a safety
 lever is lifted the motor should stop immediately after release of the
 lever. After release of the lever the motor drive should finish the
 operation.

After pushing the emergency push button B5 the motor
 protective switches should trip and the red signal should come on.

One of two condensation heaters is energized continuously
 where as the second one is thermostatically controlled and switched on at low
 ambient temperature turn the thermostat off and check the second heater
 becomes hot.

The test of the MA7 motor drive is now complete. In order to
 eliminate any possible error, a ratio of the transformer is recommended to
 compare with existing records.

The ratio check should be done on manual. Turn the motor drive
 back to the neutral position.

Set the motor drive to remote control after testing is
 complete

Introduction
We recommend a periodic inspection of the tap changer

 Also, we recommend that personnel well acquainted with the equipment should

 The Inspection should be carried out as quickly as possible with the most care
